the tectonic evolution of the Hotan region in the context of the active deformation of the Tarim and Tibetan basins.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hotan-Qirah fault system accommodates 3.5–4.5 ±2 mm/yr of crustal convergence between the Tarim platform and the Western Kunlun mountains.
the Hotan normal fault scarp is a tectonic scarp, which is not only a result of the tectonic activity but also a result of the climate-driven fluvial incision.
the Hotan-Qire fault system is an active structure that is not only responsible for the subsidence of Tarim, but also for the formation of the piedmont terraces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hotan-Qiara fault system is a major active normal fault system that accommodates a significant part of the deformation between the Tarim and the Tibetan Plateau.
the northern piedmont of Western Kunlun range has been subsiding at least 4–5 mm/yr since 12–22 ka, and the rate of convergence between western Kunlun and Tarim is at least 5–7 mm/yr.
, the Hotan-Qiara normal fault system is a part of the active tectonics system in southern Xinjiang.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hotan-Qirah normal fault system is an important component of the active tectonics of the northern piedmont of western Kunlun.
the Hotan-Qaraqash fault system has been active since the late Pleistocene, but the rate of slip is not sufficient to account for all the convergence between the Tibetan Plateau and Tarim Basin.
